grades.reason: Covers fork/exec/waitpid and zombie processes. It says nothing about copy-on-write or memory isolation between parent and child.

grades.quote: When the MMU interrupts the processor due to a write into the read-only page of zeros, the operating system can update the mapping for that one page to refer to a separate read/write page frame of zeros and then resume the process.
grades.reason: It explains the core COW mechanism: many virtual pages share one read-only physical frame, and a write fault gives the writer its own private writable frame. It applies this to zero-filling, not to fork, so it covers only part of the question. The isolation principle carries over directly.

grades.quote: Be sure to take COW into account.
grades.reason: This is an exercise list. Only exercise 7.1 touches on fork and copy-on-write, and it only asks the reader to consider COW when scheduling parent versus child. It never explains how COW shares pages or how it keeps parent and child from overwriting each other's memory. The rest of the passage covers access control and is unrelated.
It discusses lock-free shared data and memory ordering in xv6, including the parent writing the child's pages during fork. It does not describe copy-on-write sharing or write-fault isolation.
